correctness.rationale: Each private twin leaf bundle forces at least k_i-1 leaves in X. Omitting one requires its center in X; omitting none permits either center status. Distinct omitted vertices have mutually distinguishable nonempty traces by their private leaves or singleton core neighbors. This proves the iff classification; independent multiplication yields the polynomial. The complementary domination requirement forces the stated choices and counts; size-n dominating sets have precisely the same local options. For k_i>=2 the D-side cannot distinguish its omitted leaf twins. All cases, including singleton core/bundle and arbitrary disconnected H, are covered. The included verifier exhaustively tested 1335 labelled graphs and 1518440 vertex subsets, without extrapolating from them.

originality.rationale: The source 2026 EJC Theorem 6 and Corollary 7 give universal existence and bound and explicitly mention H corona K1 as a sharp example, but do not classify/count all DLDS partitions, full LD code enumerators, or heterogeneous bundles. The 2014 all-set corona characterization assumes both factors connected and nontrivial, excluding all independent-leaf bundles used here. The 2012 corona article (sec. 4) establishes minimum locating-domination numbers and bounds for ordinary corona products; those numbers cannot determine every coefficient of the LD polynomial or counts of complement partitions. Fazil et al. (2022) define the polynomial (Definition 2.4) and evaluate multipartite graphs, Petersen graph, and certain lexicographic products, but not the corona bundle factorization. Open-twin lower bounds alone leave sufficiency and simultaneous domination of complements unresolved. Searches of accessible historical claim IDs and published-finding corpus returned only structurally different invariants/families; absolute literature priority remains at risk.
residual_risks: Full text of the 2025 twin-free partitions preprint was not read; its abstract indicates different hypotheses, but details may discuss coronas.
Unindexed, inaccessible, and differently worded location-domination enumerations may exist; database search is not evidence of absolute priority.
The 2026 general DLDS paper already credits the one-leaf corona equality and existence as prior; the novel assertions are the precise all-set enumeration and general bundle-classification/counts.

Canoy et al. (2014) give a conceptually close all-set corona characterization on connected, nontrivial attached factors. It does not formally include edgeless private-leaf bundles, but a generalization of their technique may independently rediscover part of this formula.

value.rationale: Natural and independent-of-H full enumeration for every private-leaf blowup, even with heterogeneous leaf multiplicities, replaces nonconstructive bounds with a structural all-set classification. Exact enumerator gives minimum and all higher coefficients, polynomial real-rootedness, and optimal-code redundancy. The 2^s complementary-partition count and sharp two-LD criterion address 2026 questions of how domination and localization can be partitioned; the open-twin threshold at bundle size 2 is structural, not arbitrary. This is more than computing a special instance of an already tabulated invariant.
